did: Home now answers every request within eight seconds, even under your old phone's pull-to-refresh storm. A request it has no room for is told 'busy, try again in five seconds' instead of hanging until the phone gives up and says home is away. Behind that: the request queue had no time limit, the overload guard never fired, and a database wait could run thirty seconds. Home's /compat answer now tells the phone its real rate limit, so the phone can pace itself to home rather than assume sixty a minute. And a new alert, HomeShedding, tells you on Slack whenever home has to turn requests away busy.

calls.title: How long home takes before answering busy
options: 8 s, and 3 s to wait for the database
keep 15 s and bound only the queue and the database wait
calls.why: The phone gives up at 10 s, so 8 s leaves room for the network; a request body still arriving at 8 s is now answered busy, and the phone had already given up on those.
calls.undo: Raise ANSWER_WITHIN and POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT in server's apps/servers/file_host/src/admission.rs; the build refuses anything at or over 10 s.

calls.title: How long home asks a busy phone to wait
options: until the oldest request in flight would time out
calls.why: Long enough for a pull-to-refresh burst to drain, short enough that your next tap is served; nothing has measured how long a storm on home really lasts.

calls.title: Whether a busy answer pages like an error
options: log it as a warning and alert on the count (HomeShedding)
log it as an error, like every other 5xx
calls.why: An error per shed request would page once for every request in a storm; one alert over 15 minutes says the same thing once.
calls.undo: Drop the Busy case before the server-error branch in FileHostError::into_response.

calls.title: The shape of the rate limit /compat tells the phone
options: rate_limit: per_minute and burst, in snake_case like the rest of /compat
rateLimit: perMinute and burst, in camelCase
also the refill interval in milliseconds
calls.why: Everything else in /compat's answer is snake_case, and the refill interval follows from per_minute.
calls.undo: Rename the RateLimit fields in server's handlers/compat.rs, with the phone's reader in the same change.

left: server#936: low findings from #934's review, among them /ready can still report the database down when every connection is busy, and how the background loops log a 3 s database wait.
The phone should treat a 503 with Retry-After as busy, and a 503 without one (the account, pairing and ceremony caps) as a cap; that is the some-ui HERD worker's.
some-ui's ledger needs AD4, home answers within 8 s, with HomeShedding as its watch; the coordinator holds the lines.
Two wording nits on HomeShedding's text, left on server#942 rather than re-run CI for words.
